 SUIT FOR SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE, CANCELLATION AND PERMANENT INJUNCTION ALONGWITH CONSEQUENTIAL RELIEF. 
 
 
 
 WRITTEN STATEMENT OF BEHALF OF DEFENDANT NO. 2 
 
 
 
 That the Defendant No. 2 is a private limited company incorporated under the laws of Pakistan and is mainly engaged in the business of providing real estate marketing services, which, inter alia, include real estate portal, real estate classifieds, real estate advertising, organizing of real estate exhibitions and events and promoting the real estate business through electronic, print, social media and other means . 
 
 That the present Written Statement is being filed by the Defendant No. 2 through M s . Maryam Haq, its duly authorized officer, who is fully conversant with the facts of the case and is duly authorized to plead and appoint attorney on behalf of Defendant No. 2 . 
 
 [Copy of the Board Resolution is attached as Annexure A ] 
 
 Preliminary Objections: 
 
 That the titled Suit is absolutely misconceived, devoid of any merits, has been filed with unclean hands, fails to disclose any cause of action against Defendant No. 2 , is in direct contravention to express provisions of law and settled dicta laid down by the superior courts, is based on extraneous considerations and misstated facts . Therefore , the instant S uit is liable to be dismissed/rejected to the extent of Defendant No. 2 . 
 
 That the relevant facts in relation to the instant Suit are that the Defendant No. 1 entered into a Project Promotion Agreement dated 18.10.2017 with Defendant No. 2 which came into effect on 01.11.2017 (the “Agreement” ). The Agreement was for promoting and marketing Broadway Heights situated at commercial area, Bahria Town, Main Raiwind Road, Lahore based on 7.73 Kanals of land consisting of 29 commercial plots of 5.33 Marlas each, 220 residential units and 311 commercial units (the “Project” ). 
 
 [Copy of the Agreement dated 18.10.2017 is attached as Annexure B ] 
 
 
 That bare perusal of the Agreement unequivocally indicates that the Defendant No. 2 was engaged by the Defendant No. 1 to facilitate it in promoting and marketing the Project . It is highly imperative to mention here that the Agreement did not transfer an y type of interest and/or title in the Project to the Defendant No. 2. T he Defendant No. 2 is only responsible for marketing and selling the Project inventory on behalf of Defendant No. 1 . 
 
 That, addition ally, it may also be noted here that , as per the Plaintiff’s own admission, he allegedly bought the two shops No. F-17 and F-18 measuring 325 Sq. Ft. at 1 st Floor of Broadway Heights-III (the “Shops” ) in April, 2016 , whereas the Agreement between the Defendant No. 1 and Defendant No. 2 was executed on 18.10.2017 . Therefore, for all intents and purposes, the Defendant No. 2 has no nexus, whatsoever, with the dispute at hand , which is explicitly between the Plaintiff and Defendant No. 1 in relation to the Shops . 
 
 Preliminary Submissions: 
 
 That , at the very outset , it is submitted that perusal of Plaint reveals that the only alleged claim against the Defendant No. 2 is that the Defendant No. 1 sold the Project, including the Shops , to Defendant No. 2 through the Agreement. This is a misstatement of facts and misunderstanding of the Agreement by the Plaintiff. In this respect , it is submitted that the Agreement , by no stretch of imagination, tr ansfers an y kind of interest and/or title in the Projec t ( which includes the Shops in dispute) to the Defendant No. 2. Thus, it is clear that the Plaintiff miserably fails to disclose any cause of action against the Defendant No. 2 . 
 
 That, without prejudice to the above, it is submit ted that t he Agreement has a sunset clause, which provides that the Agreement is valid for a period of 2 years. It is submitted that, no agreement to sell has a define d term . This further te nds to show that the Agreement is not of sale . 
 That the instant Suit is absolutely misconceived, devoid of any merits, based on extraneous considerations and misstated facts, fails to disclose any cause of action against the Defendant No. 2 , barred by express provisions of law and against authoritative pronouncements of superior courts, hence, merits dismissal at its very inception . 
 
 Para-wise Reply 
 
 That the contents of the corresponding paragraph are denied for want of knowledge. T he contents of the preliminary objections and submissions are reiterated here. Further, it is specifically averred that the Agreement between Defendants stood executed on 18.10.2017 and allegedly the Plaintiff purchased the Shops in April, 2016. Hence, in any eventuality, the Defendant No. 2 has no concern /interest whatsoever with the instant dispute, which is between the Plaintiff and Defendant No. 1 in connection with the Shops. Therefore, the instant Suit is liable to be dismissed to the extent of Defendant No. 2 . 
 
 That the contents of the corresponding paragraph are denied for want of knowledge. 
 
 3-5 That the contents of the corresponding paragraphs are vehemently denied . The contents or preliminary objections and preliminary submissions are reiterated. The Agreement executed between the Defendants pertain to marketing and selling of the Project inventory only and the ownership rights of the Project remains with the Defendant No. 1. Without prejudice to the foregoing, the clause 3 of the booking terms and conditions (annexed with the Plaint) specifically allows the Defendant No.1 to vary, modify and alter the plans, designs and specifications of the Project. Moreover, the construction of the Project is the sole responsibility of the Defendant No. 1 as the owner of the same. Therefore, the Defendant No. 2 has no nex us with the issue in the instant matter , thus, th e Suit is liable to be dismissed to the extent of Defendant No. 2 on this ground alone . 
 
 That the contents of the corresponding paragraph are denied being incorrect. In addition to reiterating the contents of preliminary objections and submis sions, it is submitted that no cause of action ever arose in favour of the Plaintiff against Defendant No. 2. The Defendant No. 2 is only providing its services to the Defendant No. 1 in promoting and marketing the Project and nothing else. 
 
 That the contents of the corresponding paragraph are denied being incorrect. It is submitted that as no cause of action ever arose in favour of the Plaintiff against the Defendant No. 2, hence, this Learned Court has no jurisdict ion against the Defendant No. 2 in respect of the preset matter. 
 
 That the contents of the corresponding paragraph are denied being incorrect. 
 
 Prayer 
 
 In view of the above, it is most respectfully prayed that the instant Suit may kindly be dismissed to t he extent of Defendant No. 2. Alternatively, the name of Defendant No. 2 may be struck off from the array of parties under Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 . 
 
 Any other relief deem fit and appropriate by this Learned Court may kindly also be granted in favour of the Defendant No. 2. 
 
 Defendant No. 2 
 Through 
 
 Waleed Khalid 
 Barrister-at-Law

 WRITTEN STATEMENT OF BEHALF OF DEFENDANT NO. 2 
 
 
 REPLY TO APPLICATION UNDER ORDER XXXIX RULE 1 AND 2 READ WITH SECTION 151 OF CPC FOR THE ISSUANCE OF TEMPORARY INJUNCTION 
 
 
 Preliminary Objections 
 
 That the contents of the accom panying written statement be read as an integral part of this reply. 
 
 That the instant Application is absolutely misconceived, devoid of any merits, does not satisfy the ingredients of injunction, against express provisions of law and settled dicta of superior courts and, hence, is liable to be dismissed. 
 
 That the Plaintiff has failed to disclose any cause of action against Defendant No. 2 and no prima facie case is made out by the Plaintiff. 
 
 That the balance of convenience does not lie in favour of the Plaintiff, the instant Suit pertains to monetary obligations, hence, no question of irreparable loss arise. 
 Para-wise Reply 
 Needs no reply. 
 2-4 That the contents of the corresponding paragraphs are denied being incorrect. It is submitted that no prima facie case has been established by the Plaintiff. Further, bare perusal of the instant Suit indicates that the balance of convenience does not lie in favour of the Plaintiff and no irreparable loss will be suffered by the Plaintiff. On the other hand, the Defendant No. 2 has established a prima facie case, balance of convenience also lies in its favour and same will suffer irreparable loss if the instant Suit / Application is allowed to be proceeded with against Defendant No. 2. 
 In view of the above, it is most respectfully prayed that the instant Application may kindly be dismissed . 
 Any other relief deem fit and appropriate by this Learned Court may also be granted in favour of the Defendant No. 2 / Respondent No. 2. 
 
 Defendant No. 2 / Respondent No. 2 
 Through 
 
 Waleed Khalid 
 Barrister-at-Law 
 Advocate High Court
